# Write a simple legal disclaimer with DeepSeek’s chat

**Hook:**
You need a legal disclaimer on your website, but writing one feels like reading another language. DeepSeek’s chat can draft a clear, plain-English version you can copy and paste in minutes — no lawyer required.

## Before you start
- A **free DeepSeek account** (sign-up takes 2 minutes at chat.deepseek.com).
- A **text editor** (Notes, Google Docs, or Word) to paste and tweak the result.
- Your **website URL** and a rough idea of what your site does (sells things, gives advice, hosts content).
- **10 minutes** total time.

---

## Step 1 — Open DeepSeek Chat and start a new conversation
Open your web browser and go to [chat.deepseek.com](https://chat.deepseek.com). You’ll see a clean white page with a chat box at the bottom. Click inside the box and type your first message. You’ll know it worked when the chat box expands and a blinking cursor appears.
💬 Example:
`Hi`

## Step 2 — Ask DeepSeek to draft a legal disclaimer
In the same chat box, type a clear instruction. DeepSeek will reply with a draft disclaimer you can copy. You’ll know it worked when you see a block of text starting with “**Legal Disclaimer**” and ending with “**End of Disclaimer**.”
💬 Example:
`Write a simple legal disclaimer for my website. My site sells handmade candles and offers candle-making tips. Include liability, accuracy, and copyright sections.`

## Step 3 — Review the draft and ask for changes
Read the reply. If the tone is too formal or too casual, tell DeepSeek to adjust it. You’ll know it worked when the chat replies with a revised version that feels right for your brand.
💬 Example:
`Make it friendlier and shorter. Use everyday words like “we” and “you.”`

## Step 4 — Ask DeepSeek to add your website details
If the draft doesn’t include your site name or URL, ask DeepSeek to insert them. You’ll know it worked when the text now reads “**MyCandleCo.com**” and “[https://mycandleco.com](https://mycandleco.com)” in the right places.
💬 Example:
`Replace “my website” with “MyCandleCo.com” and add the URL https://mycandleco.com`

## Step 5 — Ask DeepSeek to add a copyright year
If the draft doesn’t include the current year, ask DeepSeek to add it. You’ll know it worked when the text now reads “© 2026 MyCandleCo.com” at the bottom.
💬 Example:
`Add the current year to the copyright line.`

## Step 6 — Copy the final draft and paste it onto your site
Highlight the entire disclaimer text in the chat, copy it, and paste it into your website’s footer or a dedicated “Legal” page. You’ll know it worked when the text appears exactly as you pasted it on your live site.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** The draft is too long or too short.
  **Fix:** Ask DeepSeek to “shorten to 150 words” or “expand to 300 words” until it feels right.
- **Mistake:** The draft uses legal jargon like “indemnify” or “hereinafter.”
  **Fix:** Say “rewrite in plain English” and DeepSeek will simplify the wording.
- **Mistake:** You forget to update the site name and year.
  **Fix:** Always ask DeepSeek to insert your exact details before copying.

---

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** If you run a small blog or shop, this disclaimer protects you from claims about advice or products you share.
- **For your business or work:** A clear disclaimer builds trust with visitors and can reduce legal risk.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with a simple draft from DeepSeek, then tweak it as your site grows.

---

## Try it now
Open [chat.deepseek.com](https://chat.deepseek.com), type `Write a simple legal disclaimer for my website. My site sells handmade candles and offers candle-making tips. Include liability, accuracy, and copyright sections.` and copy the reply into your site’s footer.
